arxiv-1702-03678.creator: J. M. Kashyap
arxiv-1702-03678.description: Abstract Search of life elsewhere in the galaxy is very fascinating area for planetary scientists and astrobiologists. Earth Similarity Index (ESI) is defined as geometrical mean of four physical parameters (Such as radius, density, escape velocity and surface temperature), which is ranging from 1 (identical to Earth) to 0 (dissimilar to Earth).

arxiv-2011-05216.title: Cyclic quadrilaterals and smooth Jordan curves Thanks: JEG was supported on NSF Award DMS-2005619.
arxiv-2011-05216.creator: Joshua Evan Greene, Andrew Lobb
arxiv-2011-05216.description: Abstract . For every smooth Jordan curve γ \gamma and cyclic quadrilateral Q Q in the Euclidean plane, we show that there exists an orientation-preserving similarity taking the vertices of Q Q to γ \gamma . The proof relies on the theorem of Polterovich and Viterbo that an embedded Lagrangian torus in ℂ 2 {\mathbb{C}}^{2} has minimum Maslov number 2.

arxiv-2103-09555.creator: Alberta Longhini, Michael C. Welle, Ioanna Mitsioni, Danica Kragic
arxiv-2103-09555.description: Abstract Identification of textile properties is an important milestone toward advanced robotic manipulation tasks that consider interaction with clothing items such as assisted dressing, laundry folding, automated sewing, textile recycling and reusing. Despite the abundance of work considering this class of deformable objects, many open problems remain.

arxiv-2105-06299.title: Measurement of nuclear spin relaxation time in lanthanum aluminate for development of polarized lanthanum target
arxiv-2105-06299.creator: K. Ishizaki, H. Hotta, I. Ide, M. Iinuma, T. Iwata, M. Kitaguchi, H. Kohri, D. Miura, Y. Miyachi, T. Ohta, H. M. Shimizu, H. Yoshikawa, M. Yosoi

arxiv-2110-14038.title: Robustness of Graph Neural Networks at Scale
arxiv-2110-14038.creator: Simon Geisler, Tobias Schmidt, Hakan Şirin
arxiv-2110-14038.description: Abstract Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are increasingly important given their popularity and the diversity of applications. Yet, existing studies of their vulnerability to adversarial attacks rely on relatively small graphs. We address this gap and study how to attack and defend GNNs at scale.

arxiv-2302-04267.creator: Andrea Maiani, Karsten Flensberg, Martin Leijnse, Constantin Schrade, Saulius Vaitiekėnas, Rubén Seoane Souto
arxiv-2302-04267.description: Abstract Coherent tunneling processes of multiple Cooper pairs across a Josephson junction give rise to high harmonics in the current phase relation. In this work, we propose and study Josephson junctions based on semiconductor-superconductor-ferromagnetic insulator heterostructures to engineer nonsinusoidal current-phase relations.

arxiv-2302-05039.title: Predicting Desirable Revisions of Evidence and Reasoning in Argumentative Writing
arxiv-2302-05039.creator: Tazin Afrin, Diane Litman
arxiv-2302-05039.description: Abstract We develop models to classify desirable evidence and desirable reasoning revisions in student argumentative writing. We explore two ways to improve classifier performance – using the essay context of the revision, and using the feedback students received before the revision. We perform both intrinsic and extrinsic evaluation for each of our models and report a qualitative analysis.

arxiv-2405-10161.title: Torus knots and generalized Schröder paths
arxiv-2405-10161.creator: Marko Stošić, Piotr Sułkowski
arxiv-2405-10161.description: Abstract We relate invariants of torus knots to the counts of a class of lattice paths, which we call generalized Schröder paths. We determine generating functions of such paths, located in a region determined by a type of a torus knot under consideration, and show that they encode colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials of this knot.

pmc-10694492.title: Instant processing of large-scale image data with FACT, a real-time cell segmentation and tracking algorithm
pmc-10694492.creator: Ting-Chun Chou, Li You, Cecile Beerens, Kate J Feller, Jelle Storteboom, Miao-Ping Chien
pmc-10694492.description: SummaryQuantifying cellular characteristics from a large heterogeneous population is essential to identify rare, disease-driving cells. A recent development in the combination of high-throughput screening microscopy with single-cell profiling provides an unprecedented opportunity to decipher disease-driving phenotypes. Accurately and instantly processing large amounts of image data, however, remains a technical challenge when an analysis output is required minutes after data acquisition.

pmc-11401097.title: Optimizing energy management strategies for microgrids through chaotic local search and particle swarm optimization techniques
pmc-11401097.creator: Ping Li, Qian Liu
pmc-11401097.description: The advent of multi-Microgrid (MG) energy systems necessitates the optimization of management strategies to curtail operational costs. This paper introduces an innovative MG energy management strategy that integrates Chaotic Local Search (CLS) with Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to fulfill this requirement.

pmc-11506118.title: Enrichments Adjusted to the Number of Litters: Simple Approach to Improve the Welfare of Weaned Piglets under Farm Conditions
pmc-11506118.creator: Nejc Kuri, Janko Skok, Dejan Škorjanc, Maja Prevolnik Povše, Emma Fàbrega i Romans
pmc-11506118.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple SummaryWeaning is one of the most stressful phases in intensive pig production. The mixing of unknown litters initiates the establishment of a new social order through conflicts, which are abnormally increased under commercial farming conditions due to several other sudden changes in the piglets’ environment, such as the separation of the piglets from the sow and changes in feeding and space. Providing appropriate environmental enrichment is a possible solution to mitigate stress and aggression after weaning.

pmc-11692895.title: COMPARISON OF HEALTH OUTCOMES AMONG TWO SEPTUAGENARIAN COHORTS A DECADE APART IN JAPAN
pmc-11692895.creator: Can Wang, Yasuyuki Gondo, Takeshi Nakagawa, Yukie Masui, Kei Kamide, Ayaka Kasuga, Saori Yasumoto, Madoka Ogawa
pmc-11692895.description: BackgroundPrevious studies have suggested that the health status of older adults living in the community has improved significantly over the past two decades. To reassess whether this trend continues, this study examined the health profiles of a current cohort of 70-year-olds and compared them with a cohort born a decade earlier.

pmc-12421179.title: Health facility and contextual correlates of HIV test positivity: a multilevel model of routine programmatic data from Malawi
pmc-12421179.creator: Miyu Niwa, Dylan Green, Tyler Smith, Brandon Klyn, Yohane Kamgwira, Sara Allinder, Deborah Hoege, Suzike Likumbo, Charles B Holmes, Gift Kawalazira, Linley Chewere
pmc-12421179.description: BackgroundInnovative and efficient methods are needed to identify remaining people living with HIV unaware of their status. Routine health information system (RHIS) data, widely available in high-burden HIV settings, may help target areas of high risk to deliver timely prevention services. Often underused, RHIS data were leveraged at the facility level to predict changes in HIV test positivity in Malawi.

pmc-13190483.title: Risk factors for positive urine culture and antimicrobial resistance in suspected UTI after flexible ureteroscopic lithotripsy
pmc-13190483.creator: Hongbo Wang, Wenzhi Gao
pmc-13190483.description: BackgroundThis study identified independent risk factors for positive urine culture and bacterial resistance in patients with suspected urinary tract infection (UTI) after flexible ureteroscopic lithotripsy (FURL), to provide an evidence-based basis for individualized clinical antimicrobial treatment strategies.MethodsA retrospective cohort study enrolled 864 adult patients with suspected UTI after FURL who underwent urine culture between January 2024 and June 2025.

pmc-13283547.title: Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction and Injury Risk after Second Reconstruction Surgery in Adolescents
pmc-13283547.creator: Anagh Astavans, Jay Lee
pmc-13283547.description: Background:Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tears are a common knee injury in younger populations, that can re-occur following ACL reconstruction (ACLR). Approximately 10-16% of children with a primary ACLR require revision, but the portion of pediatric patients which require an additional ACLR after a second procedure is unknown.

pmc-13390005.title: A generative framework for predicting cellular morphological and transcriptomic perturbation responses
pmc-13390005.creator: Rui Peng, Ziru Liu, Yuanxu Gao, Jinzhuo Wang
pmc-13390005.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryPredicting coordinated cellular responses to perturbations is crucial for phenotypic drug discovery and building virtual cell models. Current methods typically predict isolated modalities or require empirical post-perturbation data, precluding true de novo virtual screening. To address this, we introduce MultiVCDiff, a unified multimodal generative diffusion framework that simultaneously predicts high-fidelity cellular morphology images and transcriptomic profiles directly from chemical or genetic perturbations. This framework was trained on a comprehensive trimodal corpus encompassing 1,118 chemical and 130 genetic perturbations across four datasets.

pmc-13662685.title: Antioxidant, antitumor and antimicrobial activities of Pisolithus albus extract against some pathogenic bacteria and fungi☆
pmc-13662685.creator: Sahar M Ouda, GA Mohamed
pmc-13662685.description: BackgroundPisolithus albus is an ectomycorrhizal fungal species that commonly associates with trees, particularly in loose, sandy soil environments.Methods and ResultsIn this study it was collected, molecular identified as new record to Egypt with GenBank accession numbers, PX788599. Then the study focused on determination of capacity of the fungus to produce bioactive substances with antioxidant, antimicrobial and anti-tumor activities.
